summary:
Catalunya stands under the national framework of Spain; the region-specific layer is set by Ley 11/2014 of 10 October 2014, published in the Diari Oficial de la Generalitat de Catalunya (DOGC núm. 6730) on 17 October 2014.

Ley 11/2014 defines direct discrimination, indirect discrimination and discrimination by association on grounds of sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression or sex characteristics.

The statute obliges Catalan public administrations to establish mechanisms so that administrative documentation reflects a person's gender identity.

Its protections extend across education, health, employment and sport, and it broadens the mandate of the Observatori Català de l'Esport to act against violence and discrimination in sport.

On partnership, the statute guarantees participation in death procedures, specifically identification of the body, burial and the handling of personal effects, to a surviving partner whose relationship is classed as same-sex under the law.

Article 35 sanctions minor breaches by reference to the indicador de renda de suficiència de Catalunya, at between seven days' and three months' worth of that indicator. Article 38 places the sanctioning regime under the department competent for LGBTI non-discrimination, and the Síndic de Greuges may instigate proceedings.

Implementation of the national framework in the region falls to the Generalitat de Catalunya.
tangentialFactors:
The region's legislation precedes the national statute. The Ley de Parejas of 30 June 1998 was the first couples law in Spain to grant couples of the same sex minimum legal provisions, and Ley 11/2014, adopted sixteen years later, became the template for the wave of LGTBI laws that Spain's autonomous communities passed during the 2010s.

The regional statute's own enforcement route is administrative: sanctions are set by the department competent for LGBTI non-discrimination and calibrated to a regional income-sufficiency indicator, and the Síndic de Greuges may begin proceedings on its own initiative.
localsOnly:
Residents encounter two layers. Implementation of the national framework falls to the Generalitat de Catalunya, while Ley 11/2014 binds Catalan public administrations and requires them to make administrative documentation reflect gender identity.

The regional sports observatory's remit was widened to cover action against violence and discrimination in sport.

A surviving partner whose relationship is classed as same-sex under the law may take part in identification of the body, burial and the handling of personal effects.

Complaints can be brought before the department competent for LGBTI non-discrimination, and the Síndic de Greuges may instigate proceedings; minor breaches are sanctioned by reference to the indicador de renda de suficiència de Catalunya, at between seven days' and three months' worth of it.
outOfScopeNotes:
No region-specific record of investigations, sanctions actually imposed, court rulings, or disputes over facilities or services in Catalunya appears in the source set. The regional statute's operation is documented through its text rather than through applied cases.

The monetary value of the Article 35 sanctions is not stated. They are pegged to the indicador de renda de suficiència de Catalunya, a figure that varies with household circumstances, so the range cannot be converted into a fixed sum from the sources available.

Whether the department competent for LGBTI non-discrimination has issued sanctions, and how many complaints have reached the Síndic de Greuges, are not sourced.
